utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon to everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-06-90-T, the Prosecutor versus Ante Gotovina et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Before we continue, I expect that later today that we'll have some time for procedural issues. I see you're here, Mr. Hedaraly. I expect from you further report on P2550, because that's still due, from what I remember. I'm saying that we would have further time, because the next witness is not available until tomorrow, isn't it, Mr. Kehoe?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Zidovec, I'd like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration that you have given at the beginning of your testimony. Mr. Carrier, are you ready to continue?

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Mr. President. Before I start I should just say that yesterday I indicated that I hoped to finish during the first session. I think I will need to go a little bit into the second session with the leave of the Court, but I will try to move it along as quickly as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, well, that leaves us sufficient time, and since no other witness is waiting, I don't think that we have a major problem there. Although it is of some concern to the Chamber if we have to wait for other witnesses not being available. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Mr. Zidovec?

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Before we start, Mr. Registrar, could we please have Exhibit D496 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Mr. Zidovec, this is the order from General Gotovina, dated 11 August 1995. You looked at it yesterday, and this is the order that establishes a mixed detachment at the Military District level for clear-up operations? Were you aware that this order -- or, sorry, were you aware in any way that this order was issued or that it existed during August 1995?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I have on my screen is a document from the Split-Dalmatia police administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Sorry, P496; I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: I apologise, Mr. Zidovec. Now that you see P496 on the screen, are you aware that this order was issued or that it existed during August 1995?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not aware of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Mr. Zidovec, I just want to go through this order in a little bit more detail than you looked at it yesterday with Mr. Misetic. At the beginning of the order you can see that it states that it incorporates the Knin clear-up operations group, as part of this detachment, and it mentions six other HV operations groups. And then on page 1, point number 3, in the first point you can see that Boris Radovic is appointed as coordinator at the detachment command level, and you might recall that he was also appointed coordinator for animal, hygiene, and sanitation measures under General Cermak's order, which is P506. Just below that point 3, number 2, there is Boris Davidovic, which we heard some evidence from you yesterday on. And the next one down, Stanko Batur. The next person down is Mr. Vanjak, and he was appointed civilian protection -- he was a civilian protection member, but he was appointed as a member of the detachment command as well. Down from that, Dr. Samardzija, that was somebody that was also appointed under General Cermak's order. And page 1 in the B/C/S and onto page 2 in the English, point 3, number 6. And following you see that there are a number of different commanders of territorial operations groups that are named as members of the detachment command. And number 10 on that list you see that Major Ante Krasnic is also appointed. Do you know this person, Major Krasnic, at all?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: And Mr. Zidovec, page 2, point number 4, you can see that General Gotovina has ordered that clear-up operations groups in Novi Grad, Gracac, Zadar, Knin, Sinj, Sibenik, and Biograd all need to have -- or have to contain certain elements, and among them on the list are items 1 and 2, an operations group commander and a deputy. Item number 3, explosive experts; item number 4, a forensic technician and operative; item number 8 is a trench-digger; item number 10, five workers for clear-up of human bodies. And page 3 the English, point number 14, you'll see that another item that's listed is a coach to be supplied by the HV in order to transport civilian protection workers. Now, Mr. Zidovec, these elements are basically the same elements that you had ordered when you put together sanitation teams. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I don't know to -- I will be as vague as possible, Mr. President. But I believe a portion should be shown to the witness that hasn't been addressed if this line of questioning is going continue and I will do it in redirect if necessary, but ... I don't know how you wish me to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said a portion --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Of this order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- should be shown. Could you point at which portion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Number 6 of the order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Carrier, will you consider whether it would assist the Chamber to also show number 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Point number 6, Mr. Zidovec, just so you can see it now, and Mr. Misetic might ask you some questions about it later: Personnel and equipment for items 4.2, 4.3, 4.4, 4.10, 4.11, shall be provided by the Zadar-Knin county police administration; this should have been a police administration for item 5 and the Split Dalmatia police administration for item 5(g). And below that, item 7: "The transport professionals of the Split Military District are assigned with items 14.12 and 14.4 [sic]; 14.4 being the coach for civilian protection workers."

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Just so the transcript, I believe, Mr. Carrier misspoke; it is 4.12 and 4.14.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: And, Mr. Zidovec, on page 3 in the English, page 2 in the B/C/S, in the middle of the page just before item number 6, part of General Gotovina's order is that Captain Radovic shall determine the place or the parties that are to report under this order. And on page 3 in the English and page 2 in the B/C/S, point number 10 reads that: "Clear-up should be carried out in line with the Ministry of Defence health administration instructions, dated 15 October 1993." And for your information that's Dr. Brkic's instructions that we mentioned before. And it goes on to say under the law of international conflict, and the first priority named there, is the removal of human bodies. And on page 4 in the English and page 3 in the B/C/S, point number 12 orders daily reporting to the HV regarding this order, and you can see it is signed by General Gotovina. And at the bottom there it says "dispatch to," and the people mentioned in item 3 which includes all of the civilian protection people that were listed there. Were you aware of any of those people receiving this order?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I am afraid I can't keep pace with the four paragraphs of questions. So if I can just have a minute to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Carrier, if you would give sufficient time for those who are following, critically following your cross-examination to give time to look at the texts as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: I'll try to slow down, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If I could just have a minute. Perhaps if Mr. Carrier is can assist me. When your question is at the bottom there, it says "to," if you could just give me a paragraph number.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: I believe I said page 4 in the English, page 3 in the B/C/S. At the bottom it indicates this order was sent to -- or is it, "dispatch to" with a colon next to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Mr. Zidovec, starting where we left off yesterday, we were looking at a report from Dr. Brkic to General Cermak, dated 12 August 1995, where he is reporting on the sanitation measures that took place between August 12th -- or sorry, August 5th and 12th, 1995. That was Exhibit D30. And, Mr. Zidovec, just for your information, there's another report that's already in evidence that was sent on that same day, which is D1059, and that was sent from Dr. Brkic and a Dr. Gotovac to General Cermak reporting on the number of bodies collected, identified, and buried, during the period 7 to 11 August 1995. And in that document, those -- an October 1993 instruction from Dr. Brkic is also mentioned. There's a -- also for your information and for my friends, it's Exhibit D612, which is another report which in evidence, that one from Dr. Brkic to General Cervenko, dated 29 August 1995, where he reports on a clearing up of the terrain of human remains from 5 to 28 August 1995, related to Operation Storm.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think -- I don't want to object too many times, but I think the Chamber has previously articulated that we're not supposed to educate the witness about what's in evidence or not. If there's a question, Was he aware of any reporting from person X to person Y, the answer is, yes, fine, let's show it to him; if not, I think that's fine as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Carrier.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Yes. The purpose, Mr. President, is simply, given the position that he has taken, is to confront him with the weight of evidence is that is already in evidence in the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we usually start asking the witness about what he knows. And if there is any need to further put to him certain elements of evidence, then whether it's evidence or not, you just take him to the -- take him to the exhibit and then put it to him. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I could just seek a little clarification on that. The issue I'm having is that when I don't agree with what the position is, then I'm trying to show evidence in order to explore whether or not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, whether it is evidence or not is irrelevant. There is a document which you would like to put to the witness and whether that would be new for the Chamber or would already be in evidence or what the status of the document is, is not -- there's no need to tell the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: On that note, I understand the court's position. If I could just then explain that there are simply documents that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: That's fine. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, documents. And, yes, sometimes it might be helpful to give us a clue as to where to find it. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: And just -- there 's a document, Mr. Zidovec, and that's a report from Dr. Brkic that General Cervenko just talking about. And in this document, Dr. Brkic reported that during August 1995, he had visited the entire front line. And he's quoted as saying: "Of course, corrected what was to be corrected." And then he mentioned that others were assisting him in the process of correction. This is regarding the sanitation of human remains. And finally in that same document, Dr. Brkic had reported: "I hope that my presence, and needless to say, with the aid of all the civil defence colleagues and with all other people engaged, I helped [sic] that the assigned task be carried out thoroughly."

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if we could please call up document number 65 ter 2096.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Mr. Zidovec, what's coming up on the screen is a report dated 20 August 1995, sent from Dr. Gotovac to Dr. Brkic entitled: "Results of supervisory reconnaissance of clearing up terrain from human bodies after Operation Storm." And in that report, it's reported that this is a regular duty of the ministry of -- the health administration of the Ministry of Defence. And he goes on to say that that's the supervision of professional work which had taken place between 18 August and 20 August.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: If we can go to page 2 in the English, still on page 1 in the B/C/S, under the heading: "Work results of professional reconnaissance." You have a chance to just review that. Dr. Gotovac is talking about civilian protection's collection of human remains and whether or not it met the established standards. And on page 3 in the English and page 2 in the B/C/S, the final paragraph on those pages he reports: "In all ... cases where discrepancies from established standards were noticed, the police and civil protection staff members were given verbal instructions regarding prompt elimination of failures. During reconnaissance, we were met with good cooperation of professionals in appropriate civil protection services who assured us that all apparent failure would be eliminated as soon as possible." Do you see that there, Mr. Zidovec?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: And if I could please tender that document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I mean, I don't have an objection to the document, but the transcript goes on for three, almost four pages before the previous answer was given. And now read out a document and say, Does that say that in that the document, yes, and then tender it into evidence. I think there is nothing more than a bar table submission at this point for this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, any objection, if it would be a bar table submission?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Not if it is a bar table, Mr. President. And I would have a standing objection to if we're going to go through telling the witness what's in evidence and then reading portions of the documents saying, Does that say that in the document? As I said there's four pages of transcript before the last answer was given.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And as I said yesterday, Mr. President, I'm joining Mr. Misetic on that issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Carrier, if have you no other questions than whether the document says what it says, then there is no need to put it to the witness, unless you would want to know more of the witness, such as earlier you asked the witness whether he was familiar with a certain document, a document, which I take it in the view of the Prosecution contradicts the testimony of the witness. But to ask a whether a document which is clear in its language says what is it says, is not of great assistance as far as testimony is concerned. The document may be important. Since there's no objection, apparently against it having been tendered from the bar table, Mr. Registrar, that would be exhibit number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit number P2572, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Mr. Registrar, if you could please call up Exhibit D603, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Mr. Zidovec, this is a special report, dated 8 August 1995, from Mr. Cemerin and was issued under Povratak, and he is reporting on civilian protection activities. Did you receive this report?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This doesn't mention my name.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I didn't ask you --

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But at this moment, I cannot remember having seen this document. However, there's no reason for me to suppose that it was not sent to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: I take it from that answer your -- is it your position that given that Mr. Cemerin, who is in charge of civil protection under you, as assistant minister, if he was sending you reports during August about the sanitation proceedings, you would have got this report or this information in another form. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is right, yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: If we could turn to page 2 in the English and page 1 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: You will see there, Mr. Zidovec, that there are some times listed, starting with the number 19, and the relevant date is August 5th, 1995. Can you see there that at 1910 it's reported by Mr. Cemerin that the deputy minister had announced that "our units were entering Kijevo, Drnis, Benkovac, Vrlika and Knin." And just below that, Mr. Cemerin reports that, on the same day, at 1917 hours, Dr. Brkic called and announced that he and his people were going in first, in accordance with the agreement with Vice-President Kostovic, and that basically the units were to prepare for clearance from the next day onwards. My question is, were you aware of this situation where there was an announcement to go in, and then Dr. Brkic announced that in fact their units were going in?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I simply cannot remember this document now, now I know that at the time Dr. Cemerin was at Knin. He was preparing the organisation of activities of civil protection. But I don't deny having seen this document. But, at this moment, I cannot confirm that. But I'm still waiting for a question with regard to this. I don't see what I could say with regard to this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: The question was whether or not you were ever aware that Dr. Brkic had basically over -- seems to have over-ridden a decision by the deputy minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, that is argumentative and contrary to our interpretation of the document, so I would ask that he not argue with him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Carrier, you give a certain qualification of what is found in the -- in the document. You're invited to stick to the text of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: My question is were you aware, Mr. Zidovec, that a Dr. Brkic had made this announcement at all, were you ever aware of it, or that there was any doctor making any kind of announcement about units going in first?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, again, I would ask that he stick to the document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If there is any dispute about the way in which a document is summarised, then you are invited to stick strictly to the text and quote that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: I apologise, Mr. President. I had basically read out -- I can read it out if that would assist.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Mr. Zidovec, the document reads: "At 1910 hours the deputy minister announced that our units were entering Kijevo, Drnis, Benkovac, Vrlika, and Knin." The next paragraph below that reads: "At 1917 hours, Dr. Brkic called and announced that he and his people were going first, in accordance with the agreement with Vice-president Kostovic, and we were to prepare units for clearance which should be clearing up the area in question from the morning (6 August) onwards." Were you aware of any kind of agreement involving Vice-president Kostovic or any kind of doctor named Dr. Brkic or a doctor from the army or any kind of issue with about who was going in first in any place on the 5th of August, 1995?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not aware of that. And if you allow, I don't know to who this sentence refers; namely, at 1910 hours the deputy minister announced that our units were entering Kijevo, et cetera. Who was that deputy minister? I don't know who that refers to.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Zidovec, on page 4 in the English, third paragraph from the bottom, and page 3 in the B/C/S, Mr. Cemerin is reporting that: "On 7 August 1995 at 0945 hours, Mr. Vanjak reported that the situation in the field was exceptionally poor, coordination with the HV was unsatisfactory." And then in brackets, it reads that: "50 civilian protection conscripts were brought to HV members" -- sorry. "50 civilian protection conscripts brought to HV members travelled from Zadar to Knin for 7.5 hours so that on 6th August they worked in Knin for only two hours."

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, on that sentence, we'd like -- in the English, we'd like a translation check, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it the line between brackets which causes you concerns.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Correct. In the parentheses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we usually do not seek verification of translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I just wanted to know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- from our interpreters, but you want to put this on the record. And what we could however do is if you would read the relevant portion in the original and then we will receive interpretation, and that's not kind of verification, but it might draw our attention to a possible problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. [Interpretation] "50 civil protection conscripts led my [as interpreted] members of the HV."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I did not receive translation of your words, but interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I heard it in my ear, so I -- in English. And it's on the transcript at line 19.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There was a problem with my channel which I was on. Could you please repeat the words in the original. I apologise for not being on the right channel.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes. [Interpretation] "50 civil protection conscripts led by members of the HV."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: It is "by" not "my," interpreter's remark.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We now have received the translation. Could you put your question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Mr. Zidovec, given that clarification and what I had read to you before, and given your position that all of the work regarding human sanitation in this area was done, or sanitisation projects were done independently of the military, can you explain what it was that was just read to you about the HV involvement, at least in the report?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So the civil protection, namely the people who were on the ground at Knin and in that entire area, did count on the logistical support of the army, most of all when it comes to the provision of means of transportation. As far as I know, those agreements mostly were not honoured, even though I don't know why. In a snap-shot of the situation, the one we discussed here yesterday, Mr. Cemerin, as the head of the civil protection department and the chief operations officer on the ground, informed me about what was agreed with the HV about the provision of means of transportation to do the work necessary and mostly did not function. They didn't work well.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: If we could turn to page 6 in the English and page 5 in the B/C/S of this document. Four paragraphs up from the bottom in the B/C/S and in the English. It reads that: "About 20 bodies were picked up today in Knin," and just for reference, it's not here, but the date, I believe, is 8 August 1995. There's brackets: "(Stored in refrigeration until burial). Dr. Brkic is causing concern problems, so Cicko asked for his activity to be restricted. Until Mr. Cicko arrived, the burials organised by the Zadar-Knin police administration and by agreement with Dr. Brkic were in a common grave." My question is, were you ever aware of any kind of agreement struck in this respect between Mr. Cicko and anybody or any knowledge about an agreement or any kind of knowledge about these burials that are listed there?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I am reading this sentence correctly, then it says organised by the police administration of Zadar-Knin county, and until Mr. Cicko arrived, the burials were in a common grave. The Zadar-Knin police administration was doing -- was performing these activities in agreement with Dr. Brkic. But when Cicko arrived, I suppose that what this goes to say is that, of course, these, the things mentioned here, happened, but once the -- once the responsible person --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... finish that answer, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No I think, Mr. Carrier is right. The witness is explaining to us what he reads, apparently. If you would like to add any questions later, fine. But do you have any personal knowledge of what is described here, or did you learn about it at the time? That was the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not know about this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... you're telling us is just interpreting what you read at this moment. Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Carrier.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Mr. Zidovec, I'm -- I'm trying to understand how it would be that this Dr. Brkic would be having contact with so many people from civil protection, and you don't have any information about what was going on. Can you explain how that's possible?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It may have been possible because this was probably about operational agreements made in Knin at the time when the -- these people were representing the civil protection. Whether the people in charge of civil protection, namely the chief of department and the ministry, knew about it is difficult for me to say. But it can be clearly seen from the orders that we issued and signed that all civil protection members had clear instructions about how to go about their work. So, the concrete case mentioned here in this sentence isn't anything that I was familiar with. In our orders, we explicitly pointed out to the sanitation units to strictly adhere to the Geneva Conventions and the civil protection conventions about the manner of burying human remains.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: So is it the case that you just don't know what was happening on the ground with regard to the collection of human remains during and after Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that what you said is the meaning. Yesterday we saw a document which Mr. Cemerin sent to my attention at the Ministry of the Interior, and all activities that the civil protection had engaged in until that moment in the sanitation process can be clearly seen from it. We saw that document yesterday, so there is no need for me to explain that to you. But that document, dated 11 August, doesn't mention any one problem that you have shown in this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: So is your position that it was simply based on the information that you had, you never actually had any first-hand knowledge of how bodies were collected during that period?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not have first-hand knowledge. I got information in the reports, like the one dated 11 August.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if we could have Exhibit D353 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Mr. Zidovec, in your statement you said that there was no formal or official communication between the HV and civil protection on the collection of dead bodies and that you worked completely independently of the military. You've made some qualification regarding some logistical support. I take it that you're not aware of any separate reports coming from the HV and from civil protection that contained almost identical information about the sanitation operations. Are you aware of anything like that?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not aware of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: And if you look at Exhibit D353, which is a one-page document in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: And, Mr. Registrar, I'm not sure whether it's possible to show two documents in B/C/S next to each other. If it is possible, can I have document number 65 ter 4976 in the B/C/S next to that document, which is also, I believe, a one-page document.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Mr. Zidovec, the document with the date, August 8th, 1995, issued under Operation Povratak, from the Sibenik police administration chief, Mr. Matic, which is on the right of your screen, lists 20 bodies that were buried on the 7th and 8th of August, 1995. And if you look at the other document, 65 ter 4976, which is a document the day after, 9 August 1995, from the HV Sibenik Operations Group which is a report on the people killed, and that was filed by Major Krasnic. You can see at the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar, for scrolling down.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: And you will recall that this is the major had been appointed --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If can he finish the question, and then I'll ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Carrier, please finish your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: You'll recall that that's the person that was appointed under General Gotovina's order that we looked at earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And that is my objection, Mr. President. This document is two days prior to the order of General Gotovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: I'll rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: I apologise, Mr. Zidovec, this is the person who was eventually appointed under General Gotovina's order as one of the coordinators. Now, looking at these two documents side by side, you can see that the 20 people listed, other than items 4, 5, and 9 on the document issued by Major Krasnic, the rest of the people listed follow basically the same information listed in the Povratak document, and follow essentially the same exact order, and even for the items that aren't exactly the same, which are -- if you look at items 4 and 5, item 4 seems to correspond with item 3, and item 5 looks like it might be the same thing or pretty close. My question to you is whether or not you can explain how it is that an HV report, issued the day after that civil protection Povratak report, contains such similar information, given your position that there was no official or direct communication on these types of issues.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot comment that. I can't comment the -- or, rather, the report of the chief of Sibenik police administration was such that it can -- it in no way relates to the report that is -- was shown here on the left. We didn't know about it at all, at least I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It took me a while to find the portion of the statement, but for the record, it is paragraph 20 of the witness's statement, and I would not agree that the question accurately reflects what the witness said in his statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, it looks as if it has not influenced the answer, but it's on the record, that --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If in the future, if we are a going to cite to a statement, if we could just -- he doesn't have to bring it up. If he could say at paragraph such and such, we can then check it and make a necessary objection on time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you refer to the relevant portions of the statement, Mr. Carrier, if you are summarising the position which finally is not exclusively found in the -- in the statement but that's at least part of the evidence the witness has given.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: And just for the record, I didn't say it was in his statement; I said it was position. It was my statement of his position. I apologise; I understand the direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, there's nothing wrong with that. I didn't criticise you for that. The issue is that if you're summarising the position of the witness, then I expect that you take into account all the evidence the witness has given. And if there is a specific written portion of this evidence to be found in the statement, then it would assist the Defence and the Chamber if you would briefly point at the relevant portion of the statement. And of course if you would like to refer to transcript passages, then, of course you are certainly invited to do so. But I do understand that summarising the position of a witness does not always allow for pointing at all the various references you had in mind. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Thank you. And if I could actually have that document tendered, 65 ter 4976, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that becomes Exhibit P2573.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Mr. Zidovec, I'm going to turn to another topic. And in your 2007 statement you said that civil protection sanitation teams did not go around looking for bodies and that you were informed by the police and police administrations where the bodies were located. This is in relation to picking up bodies connected to Operation Storm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you assist us with the paragraph number, Mr. Carrier.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Paragraph 50: "The civil police would notify us of bodies that needed to be buried. There was never any discussion regarding" -- There's more. Paragraph 72: "We did not go around looking for bodies. We were informed by the police and police administrations where the bodies were located." Paragraph 74: "We were notified by the police administrations of the locations of the bodies to bury," and it goes on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: A mere reference would have done under those circumstances.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Zidovec, there are a number of Operation Povratak orders which seem to emphasise that civil protection was to immediately carry out a number of things, including reconnaissance and use words in -- there's orders that reflect words like finding, detecting, discovering the bodies, and conducting burials.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: And I can -- if my friends want to look it up, some of the exhibits I'm referring to are Exhibit D232, Exhibit D233, Exhibit D601, Exhibit D603.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: And, Mr. Zidovec, yesterday you testified that civil protection units -- you said a couple of things. First, that they were first to reach the area where the bodies were located, and that it was the HV that told you where to find the bodies. And I'm wondering whether or not you can explain this apparent change in your evidence.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I spoke on a couple of occasions yesterday in quite clear terms that the information about the location of human remains was something that we received solely from the police. There simply was no other possibility for civil protection staff to cruise the area and locate human remains. Under the circumstances, it was impossible. And given the resources we had at our disposal, it was impossible to organise. What the flow of communication between civil protection staff was, and I mean those who were in Knin, is something I have not sufficient knowledge about, in order to be able to account for how certain members of the civilian protection got by the information to enable them to dispatch a sanitation team.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Mr. Zidovec, in your 2007 statement, you said that the civil police notified civil protection of bodies to be collected. And that there was never any discussion regarding an investigation of the cause of death.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: And just let me find the paragraph reference, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It's paragraph 50, counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: And you also stated that there was no need to issue instructions on what to do, and basically in this paragraph you're talking about whether or not foul play was suspected regarding the body, because you only collected bodies where the death had resulted from combat operations. And you also stated in your 2007 statement that if there was a need for investigation, you assumed that it would have already been carried out by the crime police. And, Mr. Zidovec, during your testimony yesterday, I'm suggesting to that you no longer assumed things and your evidence changed and you indicated that -- or you gave quite a detailed description --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I mean, at this point it is argumentative. And if there are fact questions to pose to the witness, I have no objection. But to characterise the witness's testimony, and it is impossible check the assertions being made by counsel because there is no reference to transcript lines, specific references to the statement, et cetera, at this point I would object to the argumentative nature of the questioning unless there's a foundation established first with some questions and then can he put his case to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would like to invite Mr. Carrier to point as precisely as possible to the references he has in mind. At the same time, Mr. Misetic, if you want to put to a witness that his evidence apparently was not consistent because that is what you're asking about, then you can't avoid at least some characterisation of that evidence. But if could you do that in the least argumentative language you can find, Mr. Carrier. Could you please rephrase your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: You already heard the first part, and I will go about what you said yesterday. The transcript references are T19874, T19916, T19916 again. Yesterday you said, and this is different from -- or at least a more fulsome account of the investigative procedures that were carried out with regard to bodies that you didn't include in your 2007 statement. You indicated that the forensic technician basically was required to examine the body for cause of death, to fill in a detailed crime report or forensic report, and that only after that was done by the technician would the body be allowed to be buried. You also that on the basis of this procedure and the detailed crime report, the crime police would take further steps in the investigation. Now, my suggestion to you is that you never mentioned any of this when you were asked about these things by the Prosecution investigators. Specifically about establishing cause of death, and I'm going to suggest to you it doesn't make any sense given what you said in your statement that when you were dealing with the bodies, you assumed that if there was a need for an investigation, it would have already been carried out by the crime police. And I'm going to suggest to you that your most recent testimony is not consistent with what you said in 2007.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Is there a question for the witness? We've --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going object. It's just argumentative. It's a closing argument, not a question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: The question implicit is, is your testimony consistent? Apparently.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, well, the question could be how can you reconcile your statement in this respect -- [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, there's four things that counsel put to him. And is he supposed to answer all four things?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is better, Mr. Carrier, if you would take them one by one: you said this, you said that, you said that. How to reconcile these points with what you said today or -- and put him to what he said today. To some extent, you have done it, but I must admit that it could be more focussed, more to the point. Could you give it another try.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Certainly. The purpose is that it all relates to the investigation of the bodies themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: So number 1, Mr. Zidovec, cause of death. During your testimony you gave a very detailed description, and you outline that there is no obligation on the crime technician to figure out cause of death. In your 2007 statement you said that that wasn't the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Can we get a reference for that in the statement, please. Mr. President, disagree with that characterisation, and therefore --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And apparently you disagree with all of the characterisations. And at the same time we can't do without. We can't read again the whole of the portion. In your statement, Mr. Zidovec, you say there was never any discussion regarding investigation of the cause of death of these bodies we were directed to bury. Whereas, I take it that's what you want to put to the witness, that if you testified yesterday about the procedure, that is that a crime technician would go with you and would establish what the cause of death was. So apparently Mr. Carrier has some difficulties in reconciling your statement saying, Well, all these things like cause of death to establish death, that was all not for us. We just were pointed at certain place where a body was. We assumed that if there would have been any difficulty as far as the cause of death was concerned that the police would have dealt with that already. Whereas in your testimony you said, We were accompanied, our people were accompanied, and they would apparently, then, in the presence of the civil protection officers would establish whether there was any question about the cause of death. So that is not exactly the same, and Mr. Carrier is wondering how this then can be reconciled. Mr. Carrier is this -- I see Mr. Misetic is on his feet. You disagree with my characterisation as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I do. If we could look at paragraph 74 of the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then the same question arises, to what extent 50 and 74 are fully consistent.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I have no problem if he wishes a clarification of 50 and 74. But to put to him that he said -- and this is -- the objection is the question, and the question was, You said in 2007 -- sorry, you said [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I read to him literally what his 2007 --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Not your question; the Prosecutor's question. That is what I was referring to, Mr. President. And my objection was to page 26, lines 19 through 22.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... yes, but I think -- I rephrased the question more or less for Mr. Carrier. If have you no problems with my question --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- then you're invited to answer the question. The question being: What was it? Was everything already clear as far as cause of death is concerned? If there would be any need for an investigation that it would have been taken care of already, and the only thing you still had to carry out is to bury the remains; or was it that in the presence of your people, with a crime technician, at that moment, it would be determined whether there was any reason to further investigate the cause of death. That is apparently, Mr. Carrier, what is bothering you. Could you tell us which of the two it was. Because we find elements for both in your statement and testimony.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The crime technician conducted an examination of the scene where the body was found. This on-site investigation comprises the activities I mentioned yesterday, which is lifting finger-prints, preserving the scene, photographing the scene, in order to produce something that is in the police jargon called the crime report. The crime report eventually ended up at the relevant police administration. The civil protection team had nothing to do with that. Once the crime technician did his job, the sanitation team proceeded to bury the remains.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Or not, if there was any reason for a further investigation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know if, once such an on-site investigation was carried out, the remains were taken somewhere else. I only know that once the crime scene examination was done and a crime report produced, the remains were buried.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So even if there were clear signs of a not natural death, if that would have been established by the crime technician, then, nevertheless, if a report was made, then the body would be buried anyhow. Is that how I have to understand your answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which means that, if your people would go to a place where a body was found, together with a crime technician, that the crime technician would do his job and that, irrespective of what he found, your people then proceeded to burying this person. They never had to go back because the report was such that the bodily remains should not be buried but should be further -- that a further investigation needed to be conducted. Is that how I have to understand your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I don't know of a single case where, on an order of the crime police, based on such a police report, a body was taken for an autopsy or any other procedure envisaged by the police rules. In other words, once the crime technician did his job, the remains were buried.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In all cases, as far as you're aware of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Carrier.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. If I could have Exhibit D234 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Mr. Zidovec, what's coming up on the screen right now are minutes from a meeting of the heads of the crime investigation departments. We looked at a different one yesterday, so you might recognise the format, and can you see among the attendees there is was Assistant Minister Benko; and the head of the MUP crime police, Mr. Nadj. Can you see that at the top. And this is from 6th August, 1995. My question is, did you ever have any discussions with Minister -- Assistant Minister Benko about how investigations were to be conducted or instituted with regard to the forensic technicians that were to accompany civil protection?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so, because I did not consider myself capable of discussing the matter or presenting any opinions on the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Now, you can see in this document that items are listed and under agenda, item 1 is: "Handling of hygiene and sanitation measures on the ground and tasks of the Forensic Services Department regarding identification."

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: And if we go to page 2 on the English and staying on page 1 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: At the top of the page in English, it reads: "The police and the Forensic Services Department are tasked to work on the identification of dead enemy soldiers and dead bodies of civilians. "If the identification of the body is possible, the body should be buried under the established information ..." And it goes on to say: "If the identification is impossible, the body should be buried under a number." The next paragraph I'm going to summarize, but basically the requirements that the body be finger-printed, possibly taking some photographs and video, marking the time and place of discovery, and that's for identification purposes. And below that there's assignments, and Mr. Maric is assigned to be coordinator for the different police administrations and should give specific instructions regarding the identification. And that he's to coordinate with a Mr., it says there, Cemeri. My question, at this point, Mr. Zidovec, can you confirm that that is actually Mr. Cemerin?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is him.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: And you were aware that Mr. Maric was to coordinate, as it said there, you were aware of that at the time, during August 1995?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Maric was the head of the centre for forensics at the Ministry of the Interior in Zagreb, and, as such, was the person who had the authority to issue instructions like these.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: But you understood that, in 1995, during August and Operation Povratak, he was assigned to coordinate with Mr. Cemerin on those issues.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that this is a purely technical conclusion on coordination, where the issuing and use of identification tags had to be agreed on. This was an item placed by a dead body and nothing more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: So I take you were not aware --

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: I take it that you were not aware that Mr. Maric was assigned to do anything other than -- what you're saying is just supplying body tags. Is that how I'm to understand your answer?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I think that this was the only purpose of this conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm noting the time. This would be a convenient spot to break before I move to the next document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll first ask Madam Usher to escort the witness out of the courtroom. We'd like to see you back after the break, after approximately 25 minutes, Mr. Zidovec.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Carrier, the last issue about the coordination, of course, coordination is further described here. Coordination and shall give specific instructions regarding the identification. I think we should clearly distinguish between measures that were needed to be taken to identify a -- the bodily remains, and any investigations needed, in order to further establish the cause of death. That may also explain - I do not say it does, but - with the line that follows, which is the procedure of issue and use of identification plates.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: And I hope that the next document will clarify that somewhat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's all fine. But you just put to the witness that he had a task to coordinate, and you didn't say anything about -- I think what the purpose or at least the context of this coordination was.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: I believe I actually said in that respect after I had read it to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just see. Yes, but I think you read -- I think -- if I made a mistake there, I will be glad to -- could you point me at a ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Page 32, line 4, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I was -- that was not about the passage of the coordination, but it may be that you read that out.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: I think, Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... should give specific instructions regarding the identification. Then you asked whether this was Mr. Cemerin. And then you asked: "And you were aware that he was to coordinate that during the time, you were aware of that, in August 1995." Yes, and then a few lines later you said: "On those issues," referring to something that was said ten lines before, approximately, after a lot of other questions. The witness may have a better recollection of what was said ten lines earlier than I had. Perhaps I should have had it. We'll have a break, and we will resume at quarter past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Carrier, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Mr. Zidovec, while the document is still on the screen, which is Exhibit D234, under that -- on page 2 there's a heading assignment we already looked at. One of the things that Mr. Maric was assigned to was to coordinate the different police administrations, and he was supposed to give some instructions regarding the identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: And if we could turn to Exhibit P898.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: And while that is coming up on the screen, Mr. Maric [sic], this is something that you looked at yesterday. And it was issued to the crime police chiefs on August 6th, 1995, by Mr. Maric and is the operating procedure for identification. Now, on page 2 in the English, the procedure for dead bodies is listed. And you can see there, there are a number of things listed, one of the things being a form called KTO 1, in relation to finger-prints. I'm wondering if you know anything about that form.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say anything. It wasn't anything that I had to do with in my line of business.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, at some point the Prosecution will bar table that form. It's 65 ter 7333. We could do it now if time permits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I could already ask whether there's any -- would be any objection or whether the Defence teams would first like to look at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we could have a little while to look at.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and then if possible, we'd like to hear from you later today.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Could we have it marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that becomes Exhibit P2574, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Mr. Zidovec, yesterday you testified that the forensic technicians were supposed to produce detailed crime reports. And you also said that these reports ended up in the police administrations, and you said that at transcript page 19916. And if you look at the order, and we're just looking at P898 from Mr. Maric. Under notice it says: "Send forms KTO 1 and KTO 2 to this centre." And then below that, it says: "Send unprocessed roles of film of the body for development to this centre." And both of those are supposed to be sent to the attention of Mr. Maric. Were you aware that the film, et cetera, in connection to the sanitation units and the forensic technicians were being sent directly to Mr. Maric?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I know is the following. All forms filled out at the crime scene were sent to police administrations where they were used for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I don't know to who else a crime technician from a police administration would give their material, their crime reports, than to the organisation for which they worked; namely, to the criminal police or department of -- their respective police administrations.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: So you don't actually know; you're just assuming that that's where they would go.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the document that you have shown to me, it follows clearly that the chief of the forensic centre required the chiefs of criminal police in the individual police administrations to submit such documents. I cannot believe that crime technicians would send their crime reports directly to the forensic centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Well, if you're referring to the document I just showed you, they were being sent to Mr. Maric at the centre for forensic science in Zagreb, not to police administrations. Is that what you meant when you said it was clear where it was going to?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I want to say that it is obvious here that Mr. Maric's letter was sent to the heads of criminal police in the individual police administrations, and the one thing that I can conclude from that is that it was their duty to send or forward those crime reports to the forensic science centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Mr. Zidovec, was Mr. Maric the coordinator for all forensic technicians that were attached to the civil protection units?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was coordinator for the setting of procedures for identification, but the structure of the criminal police is such that -- on instructions were forwarded to chiefs of criminal police and the police administrations, and then they would pass them on along their chain of -- along the hierarchy.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Do you know if Mr. Maric was the coordinator for the criminal police, if investigations were required for any bodies collected by civil protection units that might require an investigation?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Maric was not a person who would conduct criminal investigations. The criminal -- or, rather, forensic science centre is a technical organisation. So they do their part of the work as part of a criminal investigation. So, in other words, they verify and produce evidence. That is my understanding of the work of -- of a forensic -- forensics lab in my country.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Was there a coordinator assigned for criminal police, in relation to sanitation units?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I cannot provide an answer to that question, because I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, could we please have D235 up on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Mr. Zidovec, this is another set of minutes for the crime police sector chiefs, this one held on August 7th, 1995, and you can see some of the attendees. Those included chief of crime police, Mr. Nadj, and can you see Mr. Maric's name as well. And on the agenda, item number 1 is listed as tasks in relation to clearing up the terrain. And under AD-1, which corresponds to that agenda item, it reads: "Since in the area army activity war operations are being conducted, it is crucial to carry out cleaning [sic] up the terrain in that area, and it is our task to carry out the identification of persons in the prescribed manner, and it is not necessary to conduct on-site investigations. Mr. Maric will carry out coordination of the above." Mr. Zidovec, were you aware in any way that there was a meeting of the crime police sector chiefs or that Mr. Maric was involved where they identified their task as carrying out the identification of the bodies but there was decision, or there was at least comment made that no on-site investigation was required?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Such a document -- or there was no need for such a document to reach me because it has nothing to do with the activities I was in charge of at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Your Honours, Mr. President, there are five other sets of minutes related to meetings of the chiefs of the crime police wherein Mr. Maric is involved in the meeting, and there's an agenda item related to clearing up the terrain. And Mr. Maric indicates that there aren't any problems, et cetera, in different parts, and in two parts mentions Mr. Cemerin. Given the time constraints, and -- I think given this witness's -- wasn't present at those meetings, but it is related, I'd ask to tender those from the bar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, if those documents can be identified, we'll take a look at them. We may have had an objection to bar tabling these documents. The Chamber is aware that Mr. Kardum, who was a chief of crime police in Zadar, testified as Prosecution witness. And to that extent I need to check to see if these matters should have been put to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. How much time --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It depends --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- do you think you'd need?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I need to first know what the documents are, so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I would have expected that Mr. Carrier would have informed you about the documents he intended to use.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: They are on the exhibit list. I'll read them out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: On the exhibit list. Could you please identify them so that the Defence at least knows which ones you are actually referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: 65 ter 7335; 65 ter 7338; 7339; 7340; 7341. And if it assists, I'm looking through, and I don't see Mr. Kardum's name as present in any of those. But if they could be tendered into evidence under MFI numbers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll already MFI them so that we know what we are talking about. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter 7335 becomes Exhibit P2575, marked for identification. 65 ter number 7338 becomes Exhibit P2576, marked for identification; 65 ter 7339 becomes Exhibit P2577, marked for identification; 65 ter 7340 becomes Exhibit P2578, marked for identification; and 65 ter 7341 becomes Exhibit P2579, also marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Mr. Misetic, before the break, you said that you would like have a little while to look at P2574. Any response yet? That was the document which Mr. Carrier sought to be admitted into evidence, in which ...

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, for the Cermak Defence, we have no objection. We've taken a look so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and I see Mr. Mikulicic is --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes, we have no objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the status the P2574 changes from marked for identification to admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. If I could have Exhibit D236 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Mr. Zidovec, this is a report or order from you dated 18 August 1995, under Povratak, subject: Terrain clearing up. And in the second paragraph -- or in the first paragraph, you're describing that there's a -- been a warning issued from several international organisations regarding the burial of persons killed in the course of Operation Storm that has been fully carried out yet. And in the second paragraph, you're instructing that people look for bodies, and if they find them, to have them urgently buried in the manner established in the course of the operation (shorter identification procedure carried out by the crime police and burial organised by civilian protection)." Do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: And can you explain what you meant by "shorter identification procedure."

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The shorter identification procedure, as applied at the time, meant that all activities should be undertaken that would have been applied under normal conditions; that is, at the beginning of sanitation, when it was possible, of course. But we're talking about the 18th of August, so this is about two weeks after the period or two weeks after the start of the sanitation of the ground, and we couldn't suppose where bodies can be found, if any, and what the condition of the bodies would be with regard to weather conditions.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I just wanted to know if you could actually explain what the "shorter identification procedure" was.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it means if it wasn't possible to identify a body by finger-prints, then -- then that technique not be performed due to the condition of the body, which may have been decaying already, due to the general conditions.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, could I please have 65 ter 2459 on the screen, please. And we turn --

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Mr. Zidovec, this is a document dated 23rd November 1995 from the United Nations Centre for Human Rights field office, Zagreb. And in the subject line on the first page it says: "Meeting with Zdravko Zidovec, Assistant Minister for Interior, in connection to the Security Council Relation 1019. Please find attached a report on the meeting held with Mr. Zidovec." Can you confirm that that's you and that you attended a meeting on that issue?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: And I ask that that be tendered into evidence. I don't have any further questions on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is the report attached or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you tender the whole of the document which is a four-page document.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is it of any use to put to Mr. Zidovec, or are you intending to do that, what is reported so that he has an opportunity to either confirm or deny? That might assist the Chamber in interpreting the probative value of this report. And it might be fair to Mr. Zidovec as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: I didn't intend to, Mr. President. I understand that this is actually on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh. May I take that the report is about the conversation that was held with Mr. Zidovec and whether that's an accurate report or not? Of course, I haven't seen it until now. I see that it's two full A4, two and a half full A4, in which I would expect that it will be reported not only what the reporter said but also what Mr. Zidovec said. And I take it that you want the Chamber to look at it and to consider that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Potentially in relation to some numbers. I am happy to go through it. I understand it is actually on the Gotovina exhibit list as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But if it is a conversation -- are you going to use it, Mr. Misetic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I just finished my direct, Mr. President, so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Of course, this has now been raised in cross so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Obviously I think it is a pretty good document, so if he wants to tender it, I don't have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. So if every one thinks of it as a reliable document even in terms of the role that Mr. Zidovec has given in this report -- I have got no idea; I haven't read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, just from the perspective of 90(H), if there is something in there that the Prosecution intends to rely on, I'd ask that it be put to him. Otherwise, I mean, I don't have any objection to the document coming in as a bar table or [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and there's no dispute about whether this reflects more or less what was said, or is there any challenge to that? Because that, of course, is it important for the weight --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I cannot say that, Mr. President. I didn't go through with the witness in proofing this document, so I have no idea whether the witness would confirm that this is what was said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Carrier, I consulted with my colleagues. We tried to read through it very quickly, but, of course, if the parties agree on the accuracy of the report, then the Chamber might take this as a starting point, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm checking right now. I have seen the report, but I don't see that it is on our exhibit list, and perhaps Mr. Carrier can point it out if it is. I may be mistaken, but I can't find it here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but you'll understand that if at a later stage we'd like it consider what weight to be given to it, and then if there would be any dispute as to the content of the report and the content of the meeting which was apparently held, that we would not have the witness here anymore, so therefore --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: As I indicated, Mr. President, we think that any matters of relevance should be put to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's use our time quickly to read ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Carrier, the Chamber suggests a very practical solution for the matter, which is that either during the next break or when we are dealing with procedural matters that a B/C/S copy will be given to the witness so that he can tell us whether he finds any inaccuracies in the report in relation to what he supposedly had said during that meeting, that -- and if you would limit it to certain -- to certain subjects, because it deals with killings, it deals with looting, it deals with a lot of things, then please tell us because then we could invite the witness to specifically focus his attention on those subjects.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, my only comment was going to be if quo ask for foundation for those statistics when the witness is asked questions about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes, if I see the numbers, some of them --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- approximately seem to be rather familiar to us. But I suggest that we deal with it in this way so that the Chamber knows to what extent it can rely on the report. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Zidovec, at a later moment, you'll be able to read through the document the Prosecution is now tendering, because it's a report about a meeting you had with the person reporting, and so that can you draw our attention to inaccuracies in this report, not letter by letter perhaps, but whether it reflects in -- in general what you said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we proceed for the time being, Mr. Carrier, and once we have a break, or when we're dealing with procedural matters, Mr. Zidovec will be provided with a copy in his own language. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: Mr. Zidovec, regarding your role in civil protection and fires and fire prevention, et cetera, I was wondering if you were ever aware of any order or decision made in the Ministry of the Interior to not investigate certain instances of arson or burning.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know of such a decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: And yesterday when you were testifying about reception centres, you were asked a little bit about collection centres. Is it your evidence that you don't really know anything that was happening with regard to collection centres?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to the reception centres for civilians?

utterances.speaker: MR. CARRIER
utterances.text: No, I'm asking if you recognise any difference between the words "reception centre" and "collection centre," other than the obvious fact that they're different words.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO ZIDOVEC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Collection centres were something that was completely outside of the competence of civilian protection. Our role, if any, could only have been an auxiliary one, in terms of assisting in the food supply and the provision of medical care. I suppose that you mean to say that collection centres were centres intended for prisoners or similar individuals. In such centres, if this is what you're referring to, the civilian protection did not have a role to play whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Just while we're on this point, first with respect to the five bar table documents that, a few minutes ago, Mr. Carrier tendered from the bar, P2576 MFI, to me, appears to be a document about reception centres. P2577 appears to be a document about collection centres. And to that extent if there's matters in there that relate to those issues, I would ask that if there is something relevant to that issue that it be put to him. And we cannot pull up in e-court P2578 or P2579, MFI.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Sometime there is a short delay -- or do you have the 65 ter numbers?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: We do, and we couldn't pull it up either with the 65 ter or the P number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, were you able to find the relevant 65 ter numbers?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, I was not. It appears they haven't been released.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
